purpose: Select PTGAE voice constraints by audience and content class without changing substantive authority.

registers.use: Board and executive decisions, directives, briefs, and receipts.
rules: Lead with the decision, requirement, result, or blocker.
Name the responsible office or actor when known.
Put evidence and caveats after the operative statement unless they change its meaning.

registers.use: Engineering, operations, runtime, API, architecture, and implementation prose.
rules: Name concrete systems, interfaces, inputs, outputs, versions, and failure boundaries.
Prefer verbs that describe actual state changes.
Keep provider failure, connector failure, harness failure, and application failure distinct.

registers.use: Research, theory, measurements, models, hypotheses, and assay prose.
rules: Use compact claim-status labels when evidence class matters.
Name measurement/model/assay context.
Do not replace uncertainty with vague modality; say what is unknown or unverified.

registers.use: Legal, regulatory, contractual, policy, and compliance text.
rules: Preserve defined terms and operative modal verbs.
Do not simplify away scope, conditions, exceptions, or rights.
Require substantive-owner review before final acceptance.

registers.use: Public-facing service instructions, civic information, and public-resource explanations.
rules: Use ordinary words unless the technical term is needed.
State what the person can do, what happens next, and any required condition.
Explain internal 561 terms the audience must understand.

registers.use: Customer-facing product, support, account, and service text.
rules: State the product or service effect directly.
Keep price, eligibility, limits, timing, and next action explicit.
Do not hide limitations in generic marketing language.

registers.use: Product UI, onboarding, settings, errors, and feature documentation.
rules: Use short action-oriented labels.
Name the affected object and consequence in error messages.
Do not use celebration or apology filler when a concrete next action exists.

registers.use: News, articles, publication copy, scripts, and editorial products.
rules: Distinguish reported fact, analysis, quotation, and interpretation.
Preserve source voice in quotations.
Do not turn editorial uncertainty into empty both-sides framing.

registers.use: Runbooks, work orders, handoffs, pulse receipts, and internal coordination.
rules: State current state, requested effect, receiver, acceptance, and wake.
Avoid narrative recap when a typed receipt can carry the state.
Use internal terms only when they resolve to canonical meanings for the receiver.
